samples.summary: Substantial unrequested scope beyond issue #586, only partly accounted for by the branch's own scope note. The issue's Approach is items 1–7 (errors.ts, outputError, HttpClient, throw sites, import flows, login, docs). The branch additionally ships: a ~640-line SSRF gate with IPv6-transition address rules, DNS-answer pinning via an undici `Agent`, and proxy-carried pinning with a `Host`/SNI rewrite (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts); a backend `Sec-Fetch-Site` login-CSRF control (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:144); a `runLogin` dependency-injection rewrite with a new user-facing `--allow-unbound-callback` flag; a new runtime dependency (undici) and a published `engines` bump. The task doc's "Scope taken on beyond the exit contract" narrative names only three additions (nonce, web state, browser binding) — the image gate, the pinning and the proxy work appear nowhere in it, only as checklist ticks. Each piece may be defensible individually (the lessons file argues a control must not be deferred to a branch that does not exist), but the aggregate makes an exit-code PR into a multi-subsystem security change and is worth an explicit split decision rather than an implicit one.

samples.summary: Error-matrix row does not match the code it documents. The row "Unparseable `--server` / image URL | 1 | INVALID_URL" claims a malformed image URL surfaces as `INVALID_URL`, but `assertFetchableImageUrl` catches `new URL(target)` failure and throws `blocked(...)` → `UserError('IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED', 'Refusing to fetch malformed image URL …')` before any fetch, so `fetchOrThrow`'s `INVALID_URL` is unreachable for image URLs. The exit class (1) is right; the documented `code` an agent would branch on is not.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts: `catch { throw blocked(`Refusing to fetch malformed image URL "${redactUrl(target)}".`) }` vs docs/design/cli.md:1475.

samples.summary: A new public option on a shared package's export API (`PdfFontsOptions.fetchImpl` in packages/docs/src/export/pdf-fonts.ts) is not recorded in that subsystem's canonical design doc, which already documents the `PdfFontsOptions` injection seam and the font-fetch failure behaviour. The CLI doc records the CLI-side consequence; the docs-package doc still describes `PdfFonts` as fetching with the ambient `fetch`. Nested design docs are not link-checked by CI, so nothing else will catch the drift.

`proxyForUrl` / `bypassesProxy` / `splitHostPort` / `envValue` reimplement the `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`all_proxy`/`no_proxy` semantics that the dependency being added in this same diff already ships as `undici.EnvHttpProxyAgent`. The per-hop `requestTls.servername` rewrite may genuinely need a hand-built `ProxyAgent`, but the *environment parsing* half (case folding, `.suffix`, `host:port`, `*`) is duplicated logic with its own bug surface where a library implementation exists.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/package.json adds `undici: ^7.29.0`; undici ≥6.19 exports `EnvHttpProxyAgent` implementing the same env conventions.

samples.summary: `login` terminates with `process.exit(exitCode)` while every other command in the CLI sets `process.exitCode` and lets the process drain (see output/formatter.ts:117 and the `if (result.exitCode !== 0) process.exitCode = …` pattern in docs/notes/slides/files commands). An inconsistent termination mechanism in the one command that also writes prose to stderr is an approach-fit wrinkle, not just style.

The published package's `engines` floor moves from `>=20` to `>=20.18.1`, a consumer-visible compatibility change for an npm-published CLI, driven solely by the newly added undici dependency (itself part of the out-of-scope SSRF work). Neither docs/design/cli.md nor the CLI README records the new runtime floor or why it moved.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/package.json engines bump plus `undici: ^7.29.0` in dependencies; no corresponding note in the cli.md sections this diff otherwise rewrites.

samples.summary: `--allow-unbound-callback` is introduced as a permanent compatibility downgrade with no stated removal criteria, unlike the symmetric backend-side decision recorded in the lessons file ("absent → serve and warn, hard 400 once old CLIs are out of support"). A security-weakening flag whose sunset condition is unwritten tends to become permanent; the design doc is the place to state when it goes away.

Layer fit: the "did another site navigate this browser here?" check lives inside a passport `AuthGuard` subclass, even though this endpoint already has a dedicated pre-guard layer for exactly this class of question (`CliLoginConfirmMiddleware`). Putting a generic request-provenance check in an authentication guard makes it invisible to any other state-changing route that might want it, and couples a browser-navigation concern to passport's strategy lifecycle. The design docs treat it as a first-class control, which argues for a middleware/interceptor the routes opt into.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:95 `this.assertBrowserInitiated(req);` inside `canActivate`, alongside the existing `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` for the same route.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out in full. The task doc's Approach is items 1-7 (todo.md:18-43) and its "Scope taken on beyond the exit contract" section (todo.md:45-70) names only three additions: login nonce (52), web OAuth state (56), browser binding/Sec-Fetch-Site (64). The image `src` gate, DNS-answer pin, and egress-proxy pin-carrying appear only as bare checklist ticks (todo.md:92-97, 104-107) with no scope narrative. All the claimed code exists: image-fetcher.ts is 846 lines with the SSRF gate (assertFetchableImageUrl:327), IPv6-transition rules (NAT64/6to4/Teredo:184-204), undici-Agent DNS pinning (pinnedAgent:428) and proxy Host/SNI rewrite (planHop:518-557, makeProxyAgent:469, proxyForUrl:603); backend Sec-Fetch-Site refusal at github-auth.guard.ts:145; runLogin DI rewrite with LoginDeps (login.ts:188,207) and the user-facing --allow-unbound-callback flag (login.ts:71,236); and packages/cli/package.json ships a new runtime dep `undici` (line 30) plus an `engines.node` field (10-12). Unrequested scope creep on an exit-code issue is explicitly inside this lens's lane, and no guard, caller, or issue text makes it unreachable or moot, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The "finding" is not a claim about any code in this repository — it is the review harness's own runtime error text. `scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637` (`poolExhaustedError`) produces "every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to", and `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1688-1693` (`lensFailureSummary`) prefixes it with "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict:"; `review-panel.mjs:2747-2777` then synthesises it as a severity-major record so the lens fails closed. It cites no file/line and describes no defect: it reports that the design-fit lens never executed because the credential pool drained. Nothing in the design-fit rubric (spec conformance, duplication/reuse, scope vs Non-Goals, design-doc discipline) is implicated. The repo documents this exact class of record as one that must not be re-checked as a code finding (review-panel.mjs:1682-1686, 2767-2775). Refuting it also does not weaken the gate: the lens is recorded `valid: false` (review-panel.mjs:2777-2781) and review-round-guard.mjs:187-189 pages a human on `!allValid` regardless of verifier outcome.
